claims: As of April 6, 2026, the crew of the Artemis II Orion spacecraft is in the return phase.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft slowed to around 1,276 mph during its lunar flyby.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft's initial push towards the Moon was approximately 39,472 km/h (24,527 mph).
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft had a 4,067-mile closest approach to the Moon.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft's speed was roughly 3,139 mph (5,052 kph) during its 4,067-mile approach to the Moon.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft's re-entry into Earth's atmosphere is expected on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft's re-entry into Earth's atmosphere is expected to occur at approximately 39,590 km/h (24,000+ mph).
The crew of the Artemis II Orion spacecraft is using NASA's Artemis Real-time Orbit Website (AROW) for live, moment-by-moment updates on their speed and position.
The crew of the Artemis II Orion spacecraft is returning from breaking the human spaceflight distance record.
